candidate_relations.reason: Basilar Migraine is a migraine variant, not an epilepsy syndrome. The reference diagnosis is Self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures (Panayiotopoulos syndrome), which is an epileptic condition. The clinical features (autonomic ictal manifestations, postictal confusion, normal MRI, age of onset) fit the epilepsy diagnosis better than a migraine subtype.

Panayiotopoulos syndrome (C002) is the established eponymous term for Self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures per ILAE 2017 classification. The clinical picture — 8-year-old boy, prolonged autonomic seizure with vomiting, pallor, diaphoresis, ictal confusion/dysarthria, postictal headache, normal MRI, prior similar episode — is classic for this syndrome. The two labels are complete equivalents.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Panayiotopoulos syndrome is the eponymous name for Self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures

candidate_relations.reason: Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome with Abdominal Migraine is a migraine-spectrum/functional GI diagnosis. The neurological ictal features (dysarthria, lack of eye contact, confusion, diaphoresis) and postictal state are not explained by this diagnosis, which conflicts with the epilepsy reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Migraine/functional GI disorder vs. epilepsy syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: Abdominal Migraine does not account for the ictal neurological features (dysarthria, confusion, lack of eye contact, diaphoresis) or postictal state. It is a migraine-spectrum diagnosis conflicting with the epilepsy reference.

Abdominal epilepsy is a broader, older descriptive term for epilepsy with abdominal manifestations. It is compatible with the epilepsy family but lacks the specific syndrome designation (self-limited, autonomic, childhood-onset) required by the reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broader/older epilepsy category lacking syndrome specificity

candidate_relations.reason: Acute confusional migraine is a migraine diagnosis. While confusion is present, the prominent autonomic ictal features (vomiting, pallor, diaphoresis, dysarthria, lack of eye contact) and postictal pattern are more consistent with Panayiotopoulos syndrome than a migraine variant.

Migraine with brainstem aura with confusional state and transient hypertension remains a migraine diagnosis. The reference is an epilepsy syndrome; this candidate conflicts in fundamental diagnostic category despite sharing some symptom overlap.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Migraine subtype with added descriptors vs. epilepsy syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: Migraine with aura is a migraine diagnosis and conflicts with the epilepsy reference. It also lacks specificity for the autonomic seizure syndrome.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Broad migraine category vs. epilepsy syndrome
